title: Pharma on-prem POC: requirements, constraints & workshop follow-ups
content:
Context:
- Customer: mid-size pharma R&D (computational chemistry + clinical note ingestion).
- Goal: validate Redwood Private in an air-gapped on-prem environment for inference of de-identified clinical notes and molecule scoring models.
- Constraints called out in kickoff workshop (2025-10-07): strict egress controls, HSM for keys, annual audits, no external container registries, limited on-site ops headcount.

Summary of requirements (functional + non-functional):
1) Data & security:
   - All PHI must stay on-prem; network egress == 0 by default.
   - KMS/HSM requirement (FIPS 140-2 level): hardware HSM preferred; cloud KMS not allowed.
   - Audit logging retained for 7 years; logs must be exportable to customer SIEM (Splunk).
   - RBAC integrated with customer AD/LDAP.

2) Networking & topology:
   - Air-gapped zone with a jump-host for admin.
   - Image bootstrap via vendor-supplied USB / private registry pulled from staging network.
   - Required ports (discussion): 6443 (k8s API internal), 80/443 for internal LB, 22 for jump-host, 123 for NTP (allowed to talk to internal NTP only).
   - No internet DNS resolution from inference subnet; split-horizon DNS needed.

3) Infra sizing & GPUs:
   - Initial POC size: 3 inference nodes x A100-equivalent (estimated throughput target: 25 qps for 4k-token multimodal model with async batching).
   - Control plane: 3 control nodes (VMs) for HA; storage: 20TB Ceph/Rook for model artifacts + KV cache snapshots.
   - Expectation: cold-start model load time ~ 30s with local SSD cache warmup.

4) Software & packaging:
   - Must support air-gap install via TAR bundles + local Helm chart registry.
   - Supported OS: RHEL 8.6 or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (customer prefers RHEL).
   - Container runtime: containerd (k8s v1.26 tested); SELinux permissive recommended during POC then strict in production with explicit policy tests.
   - Offline model quantization toolchain must run in isolated build environment (we will provide scripts).

5) Compliance & validation:
   - Provide evidence for: data residency, key custody, operator access logs, model input/output redaction checks.
   - Need a small eval harness that can be run locally to verify deterministic outputs w/ pinned model version.

Open questions (from workshop and follow-ups):
- Certificate management: customer asks for automatic rotation via their internal PKI. Can Redwood Private integrate with their SCEP/PKI? (Action: Investigate; assignee: Ethan)
- Update cadence: how do we push security patches without egress? Proposed: customer accepts signed offline bundles delivered via secure media + checksum verification. Confirm trust model. (Action: Lena)
- HSM integration details: which HSM vendors are acceptable? Do they require CloudHSM-like APIs, or PKCS#11 only? (Action: Marcus to collect vendor list)

Workshop notes / raw fragments: 
- Customer engineer: "We can provision a small colo rack and a dedicated subnet; security team will PCB-review any USB media."
- Ops: "We want minimal operator steps during a failover; prefer automated leader election & node replacement via node-annotations and k8s operators."
- PM: "We need a 2-week sandbox period followed by a 6-week performance soak before committing to Dedicated."

Risk log (quick):
- Risk: Offline bootstrap complexity -> Mitigation: Provide a tested offline installer + prebuilt VM images.
- Risk: HSM procurement delay -> Mitigation: Allow software KMS fallback for POC with strict audit and customer-approval.
- Risk: Model size > local SSD -> Mitigation: model sharding / quantization and recommend NVMe caches on each node.

Action items (owner, due):
- Ethan: confirm PKI integration options and draft a minimal cert rotation flow (due 2025-10-13).
- Marcus: vendor HSM compatibility matrix + procurement timeline (due 2025-10-16).
- Lena: offline bundle verification spec + checksum signing process (due 2025-10-12).
- Priya: prepare POC runbook (install steps, smoke tests, rollback) and share for internal review (due 2025-10-15).

POC acceptance criteria (draft):
- Deployment can be completed with zero internet access using our offline bundles and local registry.
- Inference cluster meets baseline throughput target (25 qps at defined latency SLO) for 48-hour soak.
- Keys stored and used via HSM (or approved software fallback) and key operations are audited.
- Customer can run local eval harness and reproduce pinned outputs.

Notes for next meeting (2025-10-14):
- Bring proposed offline bundle packaging spec.
- Present preliminary hardware list and cost estimate.
- Demo a local cert rotation via PKCS#11 mock.

Appendix / quick references:
- Internal playbook links: CONFLUENCE:PHARMA-POC (linked above).
- Related Jira: PROJ-1287 (POC tracking), SRE-2045 (k8s airgap install scripts).
- Example command snippets we discussed:
   - tar + sha256sum signing workflow (local airgap): "tar czf redwood-bundle.tar.gz ./charts && sha256sum redwood-bundle.tar.gz > bundle.sha256"
   - offline registry mirror suggestion: "skopeo copy docker://gcr.io/redwood/base:latest dir:/tmp/registry-mirror --all"

Free-form notes (scratch):
- Consider a "mini-redwood" footprint for validation: 2 GPUs + 1 control node to reduce hardware friction for early proof.
- Customer asked about telemetry: propose a per-route opt-in telemetry endpoint that writes only operator metrics, no payloads.
- Need to confirm encrypted snapshot transfer process for future migrations.

End of notes.
